## Highlights

This release makes `refresh_state()` report what it reads, and lets callers refresh only the attributes they need.

### `refresh_state()` notifies callbacks (#332)

`refresh_state()` now caches the values it reads and notifies the callbacks of every refreshed attribute once per call, even when the values did not change. Attributes that report commands (button presses, `requested_*` values, a cover's `target_position`) are refreshed without notification. In Home Assistant, `update_entity` therefore updates all entities of the channel, not only the one named in the action.

### Refresh only the requested attributes (#335)

`refresh_state()` accepts an optional `attributes` argument with callback-attribute names, the same names used by `register_callback()`. Channels that map their attributes to datapoints read only the datapoints behind those attributes. For example, `refresh_state(attributes=["force"])` on a wind sensor makes one request instead of three. Only the requested attributes are refreshed and notified, so other attributes of the channel keep their current values.

- The wind sensor and air quality sensor support this so far. Other channels, and any attribute without a mapping, still refresh every datapoint.
- Calling `refresh_state()` without `attributes`, or with an empty list, refreshes everything as before.
- A single string, such as `refresh_state(attributes="force")`, is treated as one attribute name.
- An unknown attribute name raises `UnknownCallbackAttributeException` before any request is sent.

### `UnknownCallbackAttributeException` message

The message no longer assumes the attribute was being registered, and the "atrribute" typo is fixed. It now reads, for example, `Unknown callback-attribute 'not_there'; known callback-attributes: 'state,alarm,force'.`
